about: Every word both apps put on screen. One entry per key: `text`, or a `count` argument and one template per CLDR plural category (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). `{name}` is a placeholder. `surface` is where it is drawn, and copy/surfaces.json holds each surface's length budget. `apps` says which app uses it; `example` is the arguments the fixture and the budget render it with. Design: LANGUAGE.md §2.

unit.quarts.note: US liquid quarts: the Imperial water unit in region US.

unit.pints.note: Imperial pints: the Imperial water unit outside region US.

readout.sub.coldAssumes.text: about {boil} to boil, based on history

readout.sub.coldAssumes.info.note: The name of the (i) beside readout.sub.coldAssumes.

readout.sub.coldAssumes.more.note: What "based on history" means. True to estimateTimeToBoil and rememberBoil in src/core/policy.ts: keyed by water volume, each boil blended 50/50, else the nearest volume scaled by litres.
readout.sub.coldAssumes.more.text: Each time you tap Full rolling boil on a cold-water start, I note how long the water took, and blend it half and half with what I had for that much water. I can't tell your pots apart, only how much water is in them. If I've never timed this much, I scale from the nearest amount I have. Tap the boil today and I'll correct the time while the eggs cook.

readout.sub.coldGuesses.text: I'm guessing {boil} to boil — tap when it does

readout.sub.standing.text: for this much water with the lid on ({water}) — measure the water, it changes the time

readout.sub.hot.text: from eggs in to eggs out

readout.sub.idleCold.text: from eggs into cold water, heat on, to eggs out

readout.sub.idleHot.text: from eggs into boiling water to eggs out

readout.sub.heating.text: {elapsed} heating · I expect {boil} until you tap

readout.sub.heatingEstimate.text: my guess until you tap Full rolling boil

readout.sub.coolingPeak.note: E4: the countdown ends when the model has the yolk's centre at its hottest.
readout.sub.coolingPeak.text: until the middle of the yolk stops warming

readout.sub.coolingProbe.note: E4: as coolingPeak, for a cook who said they have a probe thermometer.
readout.sub.coolingProbe.text: until the middle of the yolk stops warming — have the probe ready

readout.sub.done.text: that is the egg you asked for

readout.alarm.denied.text: no notification permission — keep the app open

readout.alarm.failed.text: the alarm did not take — keep the app open

readout.alarm.set.note: {time} is a time of day with seconds, in the locale's own clock.

readout.restored.text: Picked this cook back up after a reload. The deadlines are right, but the alarm went with the old page — keep this tab open, or Cancel and start again.

refusal.whiteNeverSets.text: With the heat off, the water cools before the white sets, so no setting works. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.harderThanPan.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.harderThanPan.text: With the heat off, this much water ({water}) cools before the yolk gets there. Firmest possible: {limit}. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.counter.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.counter.text: Resting on the counter keeps cooking the yolk. Softest possible: {limit}. An ice bath would leave the egg softer.

refusal.tap.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.tap.text: A cold tap doesn't cool the egg fast enough to stop the yolk. Softest possible: {limit}. An ice bath would leave the egg a little softer.

refusal.unlikelySoft.note: The slider was moved up to the softest level whose odds are at least 3 in 10 (reach.ts). The limit is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.unlikelySoft.text: The softest I get right at least {hits} times in {of}, so far: {limit}.

refusal.unlikelyHard.note: As unlikelySoft, at the firm end.
refusal.unlikelyHard.text: The firmest I get right at least {hits} times in {of}, so far: {limit}.

refusal.ice.note: {limit} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.
refusal.ice.text: Any shorter and the white is still raw. Softest possible for this egg: {limit}.

action.hint.cold.text: eggs in the pan, lid on, then tap

action.hint.hotStanding.text: eggs into boiling water, then lid on and heat off

action.hint.hotBoiling.text: water at a full rolling boil, and kept there for the whole {time}

action.hint.whiteNeverSets.text: nothing to start: with this much water the white never sets

action.hint.heating.text: wait for the whole surface to roll

action.hint.heating.info.note: The name of the (i) beside action.hint.heating.

action.hint.heating.more.text: A full rolling boil is when the whole surface is heaving and stirring doesn't calm it, not the first bubbles at the edge. The rest of the cook is timed from your tap, and it teaches me how fast your stove boils water, so a few seconds either way is fine, but a minute early isn't. Until you tap, the countdown is my guess.

action.hint.heatingStanding.text: wait for the whole surface to roll, then lid on and heat off

action.hint.cookingBoiling.text: keep it at a full boil ({boiling}) until the eggs come out

action.hint.pull.text: cooling starts on its own in {seconds} s

spoken.minutesSeconds.note: {minutes} is spoken.minutes and {seconds} is spoken.seconds, each already in the form its number needs.

spoken.probe.text: Now push the probe to the middle of the egg.

spoken.sousVide.note: {when} is the start phrase, lower-cased by the app.

example.subline: at 8:47 AM — 22 h 43 min at 136 °F, to eat now

controls.egg.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside the egg in the setup sentence (UI.md section 4).
controls.egg.more.text: The heat has to reach the middle of the egg, and a bigger egg's middle is further from the water. A size from the box covers eggs of quite different weights, so if you have kitchen scales, weigh one and type the weight in, and I'll use that instead of the box.

controls.measure.legend.text: Or measure the egg — fill in any one

controls.measure.hint.text: A kitchen scale is the accurate one. Otherwise wrap a strip of paper round the fattest part and measure the strip — easier than trying to caliper an egg. The other two boxes follow from whichever you fill in.

controls.eggFrom.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Egg from (UI.md section 4).
controls.eggFrom.more.text: A fridge keeps its eggs at much the same temperature every day, so I know where a fridge egg starts. A room can be a few degrees warmer or cooler than I assume, and every degree moves the time a little. If you know better, pick Custom and tell me. An egg that has been sitting out is at room temperature, so it also tells me how warm your kitchen is, which matters when the eggs rest on the counter or the heat goes off.

controls.eggFrom.hint.text: Assumed temperatures — fridge: {fridge}, room: {room}. Pick Custom if yours differ.

controls.start.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Start (UI.md section 4). Replaces controls.start.hint.
controls.start.more.text: Boiling water: lower the eggs into water that's already at a full boil, and the clock starts as they go in. They peel more easily. Cold water: eggs in a cold pan, heat on, and you tap when it boils, which teaches me how fast your stove boils water. They're done sooner, counting the wait for the boil. Sous-vide: I'll tell you when you should have started. It's usually a while ago.

controls.start.hintSousVide.note: Retired from the web by the owner, 27 September: it narrates what the screen visibly did. Delete when iOS follows the redesign.
controls.start.hintSousVide.text: A bath needs no pan, so the pan controls are put away. Your settings are kept and come back when you pick a pan again.

controls.afterTheBoil.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside After the boil (UI.md section 4). Replaces controls.afterBoil.hint on the web; iOS's explainHeatOff and explainHold say the same in two halves.
controls.afterTheBoil.more.text: Keep boiling: the burner holds the water at a full boil until the eggs come out, and how much water there is hardly matters. Heat off, lid on: once the eggs are in boiling water, turn the burner off, put the lid on, and the hot water finishes the eggs as it cools. That saves energy, but the water is doing all the work, so how much there is decides the time, and with too little it can't finish the job. Measure it if you choose this.

controls.afterBoil.explainHeatOff.text: Lid on and burner off: the water's own heat finishes the eggs. I work out the time from the water below, so measure it — more or less water changes the time, or whether it works at all.

controls.afterBoil.explainHold.text: The burner holds the water at a rolling boil for the whole cook.

controls.cooling.note: The heading of the cooling choice, opened from the setup sentence. iOS says controls.then.

controls.cooling.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Cooling (UI.md section 4).
controls.cooling.more.text: When the eggs come out, the heat in the white keeps moving inward, and the yolk goes on cooking for a few minutes. Ice water takes the heat away fastest, so it stops that soonest and lets me offer the softest yolks; a cold tap is nearly as good. Still air barely takes heat away at all: to a hot egg on the counter it is less a way of cooling than a lid. I allow for that, but it rules out the softest yolks, and how much more the yolk cooks is hard to predict.

controls.water.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Water (UI.md section 4).
controls.water.more.text: How much water goes in the pan, not counting the eggs. It matters most with the heat off, when the water's own heat does the cooking: more water holds its heat longer. It matters a little with the heat on, because cold eggs going into boiling water cool a little water more than a lot. And I remember how long it takes to boil each amount you use, so it's worth measuring.

controls.eggsInPan.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Eggs in the pan (UI.md section 4).
controls.eggsInPan.more.text: How many eggs go in together. Cold eggs take heat out of boiling water as they go in, and more eggs take more, so the water takes longer to recover, or with the heat off never does. For eggs that start in cold water it makes no difference to my sums: you tap when the water boils, and that already counts them.

controls.altitude.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Altitude (UI.md section 4).
controls.altitude.more.text: Higher up, the air presses down less, so water boils cooler, and cooler water cooks more slowly. It adds up: a kitchen up a mountain needs noticeably longer than one by the sea. Tell me roughly how high you are, and I'll cook at the boiling point shown here.

controls.settings.note: The page (web) or group (iOS) of settings that belong to the kitchen rather than the egg: units, altitude, water, eggs in the pan, heat after the boil, the probe, and what I've learned (UI.md).

help.link.note: Opens the Help page, from the top of the egg and Kitchen pages.

help.how.p1.text: I don't use a table of minutes. I work out how heat moves from the water into the egg, layer by layer, from the shell to the middle of the yolk, using the size you give me, where the egg starts, and how hot your water boils where you live.

help.how.p2.text: Egg proteins don't set at one temperature. They set with heat and time together: a yolk held a little cooler for a little longer ends up much like one held hotter for less. So I add up the heat and time the middle of the yolk gets, and stop when it has had what your doneness asks for, as long as the white has set too.

help.how.p3.text: The cooling is part of the cook. When the egg comes out, the heat already in the white keeps flowing inward, and the yolk goes on cooking for a few minutes. I count that in, which is why I ask how you cool your eggs, and why the countdown carries on after they're out: it ends when the middle of the yolk stops warming.

help.learn.title.text: What I learn, and from what

help.learn.p1.text: At first I know only what's true of eggs in general. Each egg you tell me about teaches me about yours. I keep what I learn in this browser and nowhere else, so another browser, or clearing this site's data, starts me again from scratch.

help.learn.p2.text: "How was the yolk?" teaches me your taste: what you mean by just right. "And the white?" teaches me how your whites set, which the yolk alone can't. Either answer also tells me how fast heat gets into your eggs, a number that quietly covers a lot: the eggs themselves, how hard your water really boils, a fridge that runs warm.

help.learn.p3.text: A probe reading is the quickest teacher: one number from the middle of one yolk tells me how fast heat gets into your eggs. Tapping Full rolling boil on a cold-water start teaches me how long your water takes to boil, for that much water. And only eggs rested on the counter teach me how fast the counter cools them.

help.learn.p4.text: Every question is optional. An egg you say nothing about teaches me nothing, but it costs nothing either. If I've learned something wrong, a few more eggs wash it out; Forget, on the Kitchen page, starts me again.

help.reliable.intro.text: The biggest lever is time: tell me how each egg came out, and my times close in on yours. The rest depends on how you cook.

help.reliable.forYou.note: Above the advice.* lines that would raise the odds of the setup on screen; shown only when they are low.
help.reliable.forYou.text: For the eggs you've set up now

help.reliable.every.text: Weigh the egg. A size from the box covers eggs that need quite different times, and size matters in every method. Use eggs straight from the fridge: I know how cold a fridge is, and I have to guess at a room.

help.reliable.hot.text: The simplest to get right. Lower the eggs into water at a full rolling boil and keep it there. Cold eggs cool the water a little as they go in, and more water cools less, but with the heat on it soon recovers, so the amount hardly matters.

help.reliable.cold.text: Eggs in the pan, cold water, lid on, heat on, and tap Full rolling boil when the whole surface rolls. The first time, I guess how long that takes; after that I remember, for that much water. Tap when it truly rolls: the rest of the cook is timed from your tap.

help.reliable.heatOff.text: The water does all the cooking, so how much of it there is matters more than anything else. Measure it, and use more rather than less: more water holds its heat longer, and small differences in how fast it cools matter less. With too little, I'll tell you I can't finish the job.

help.reliable.cooling.text: This matters most for soft eggs. Ice water stops the yolk soonest and most predictably. A cold tap is nearly as good, as long as it keeps running. On the counter the yolk keeps cooking for longer than you'd think, by an amount that is hard to predict, so the softest yolks are out of reach there. For a hard egg, the counter is fine.

help.odds.p1.note: Written for the direction line under the time and the range bracket under the slider (UI.md, As built).
help.odds.p1.text: No egg timer can promise the egg you pictured, and neither can I. What I can tell you is which way it's likely to go wrong, if it does: softer or firmer than you like. The bracket under the doneness slider shows the range your yolk will probably land in. The narrower it is, the surer I am, and it narrows with every egg you tell me about.

help.odds.p2.text: Behind that is a number, such as 7 in 10: how often I expect an egg cooked this way to come out as you asked, with the white set and the yolk just right by your own answer. It starts low, around 2 in 10, because before your first egg I don't know your taste, your eggs or how hard your water really boils. The time I give is the one with the best odds, which isn't always my average guess.

help.odds.p3.text: The shading on the doneness slider follows the same odds: the stronger it is, the more often that doneness comes out right. Once I get any doneness right at least 3 times in 10, I stop offering the ones I'd get right less often.

help.unsure.counter.text: The counter. How fast an egg cools in still air is the least measured number I use: nobody seems to have published the middle of a hot egg after it leaves the water. I start from the physics, and I learn it only from eggs you rest on the counter.

help.unsure.heatOff.text: Heat off. I work out how fast the water cools from how much there is, assuming an ordinary pan with its lid on. A wide shallow pan, a heavy pot or a missing lid will cool differently, and I won't know until you tell me how the eggs came out.

help.unsure.white.text: Whites. A white that sets late and a cook who calls a tender white runny look the same to me, so I learn one number for both.

help.unsure.sousVide.text: Sous-vide. Below {floor} the white stays liquid and moves about inside the shell, which my sums leave out, so I'm not reliable there. The long answer is real, though: at those temperatures the white takes the better part of a day to set.

nav.back.note: Leaves the Kitchen or Help page for the page it was opened from.

learned.title.note: The heading over learned.* on the Kitchen page.

more.about.note: The name of an (i) button to a screen reader. {label} is the control's own label, as it is shown; a language that must decline it can rewrite around it, e.g. with a colon.

setup.sentence.note: The setup as one sentence; each placeholder is a setup.* fragment drawn as a button that opens that choice. Reorder freely. Each fragment carries its own preposition and article, so in English this template is only punctuation; if your language needs the fragments in a particular case, write them in that case.

setup.sentenceSousVide.note: As setup.sentence, for sous-vide, where the egg comes from and how it cools change nothing.

setup.egg.note: Opens the sentence. {mass} is a size class's mass or a measured egg's, with its unit. Plural, so English needs no article before a number ("a 68 g", "an 80 g").

setup.start.coldStanding.note: A cold start with the heat off at the boil (the Kitchen page's setting).
setup.start.coldStanding.text: into cold water, brought to the boil and left to stand

setup.start.hotStanding.note: A boiling-water start with the heat off (the Kitchen page's setting).
setup.start.hotStanding.text: into boiling water and left to stand

setup.clause.note: The name of a clause of the setup sentence to a screen reader. {label} is the choice's heading, {value} the option chosen, both as shown.

setup.close.note: Closes a choice opened from the setup sentence.

idle.welcome.note: Under the setup sentence before any egg or boil has been learned from, when there is no refusal or advice to show.
idle.welcome.text: Our first egg together. Until you tell me how one comes out, I go by what's true of eggs in general, not yours. Afterwards, answer the two questions and I'll start learning your eggs and your kitchen.

controls.units.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Units (UI.md section 4).
controls.units.more.text: Metric or Imperial, for every number I show and every number you type. I start with what's usual where your browser says you are. Switching changes only how I write the numbers: the egg and the times stay exactly the same, and the eggs don't mind which.

controls.probe.hint.text: When the cooling ends, I'll ask for one reading from the middle of the egg. From a single egg, that tells me how fast your eggs heat.

controls.thermometer.note: The heading of the probe setting on the Kitchen page; its checkbox says probe.offer.yes.

controls.thermometer.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Probe thermometer (UI.md section 4). Says what controls.probe.hint says, and why.
controls.thermometer.more.text: If you have a probe thermometer, I'll ask for one reading when the cooling countdown ends. That's the moment the middle of the yolk is at its warmest, so push the tip to the very middle and tell me the highest number you see: anywhere else, or any later, reads lower. From that single egg I learn how fast heat gets into your eggs. I don't ask when the eggs rest on the counter, because nothing is counted down.

pan.measured.text: Based on history with this much water. I update it each time you tap the boil on a cold-water start.

pan.unmeasured.text: Tap the boil on a cold-water start and I'll remember for next time.

odds.hitTheMark.note: E5: the posterior predictive chance that the white is not runny and the yolk is just right, in tenths. Also drawn beside the time on iOS. The web leads with outcome.* instead, and says the number in outcome.odds.

odds.info.note: The name of the (i) button beside the odds, which shows odds.why in place.

odds.why.note: Under the odds, when (i) is pressed. Why a fresh install reads about 2/10, and what raises it.
odds.why.text: Before your first egg I don't know your taste, your eggs or your kitchen, so I can't be sure, and this number starts low. Each egg you tell me about makes me surer, and the number goes up.

odds.shown.note: VoiceOver's value for the (i) button while odds.why is showing. The web says it with aria-expanded.

odds.hidden.note: VoiceOver's value for the (i) button while odds.why is put away.

outcome.likely.note: Under the time, in place of the odds: the yolk is answered just right at least half the time, and a miss is as likely either way. src/ui/outcome.ts has the thresholds.

outcome.likely.firm.note: As outcome.likely, and a miss is at least 1.5 times likelier to be too firm than too soft.
outcome.likely.firm.text: Probably just right. If not, more likely a little firm.

outcome.likely.soft.note: As outcome.likely, and a miss is at least 1.5 times likelier to be too soft than too firm.
outcome.likely.soft.text: Probably just right. If not, more likely a little soft.

outcome.unsure.note: The yolk is answered just right less than half the time, and a miss is as likely either way: a fresh install, at every level.
outcome.unsure.text: Could come out softer or firmer than you like — I can't call it yet.

outcome.miss.firm.note: The yolk is answered just right less than half the time, and a miss is at least 1.5 times likelier to be too firm.
outcome.miss.firm.text: It could miss, and if it does, more likely firmer than you like.

outcome.miss.soft.note: The yolk is answered just right less than half the time, and a miss is at least 1.5 times likelier to be too soft.
outcome.miss.soft.text: It could miss, and if it does, more likely softer than you like.

outcome.whiteRunny.note: Under the direction, when at least one white in five is answered runny.
outcome.whiteRunny.text: The white might still be runny.

outcome.odds.note: The number the web moved out of the headline, first in what the odds (i) opens, before odds.why: the chance the white is not runny and the yolk is just right, in tenths.
outcome.odds.text: About {hits} in {of} eggs like this come out just as you like them, with the white set.

outcome.range.note: The bracket under the doneness slider, to a screen reader: the 10% and 90% points of the yolk, each as the nearest doneness word.

outcome.range.one.note: As outcome.range, when both ends are nearest the same doneness word.

advice.toggle.note: Under low odds. On iOS it opens the advice.* lines in place; on the web it is a link to Help, at help.reliable.
advice.toggle.text: How to make this more reliable

advice.fridge.note: Shown when the egg is taken to be at room temperature.
advice.fridge.text: Use eggs straight from the fridge. I know how cold a fridge is; a room can be a few degrees either way, and that moves the time.

advice.weigh.note: Shown when the egg is a size from the box.
advice.weigh.text: Weigh the egg instead of picking a size. One size on the box covers eggs that need quite different times.

advice.ice.note: Shown when the eggs rest on the counter and ice would raise the odds at this level.
advice.ice.text: Put the eggs straight into ice water when they come out. On the counter the yolk keeps cooking, by an amount that is hard to predict.

advice.moreWater.note: Shown with the heat off when twice the water would raise the odds at this level.
advice.moreWater.text: Use more water. With the heat off, more water holds its heat for longer, so small differences in how fast it cools matter less.

odds.stillLearning.note: E5: beside the time, for a cook's first few eggs: while the 80% range of the time on screen is wider than 15 s either way.

odds.stillLearning.info.note: The name of the (i) beside odds.stillLearning.

odds.stillLearning.more.text: My time for this egg could still be out by more than I'd like. I learn your taste in yolks from how you say they came out, how your whites set from the second question, how fast heat gets into your eggs from both, and how long your water takes to boil when you tap the boil. Answer both questions after each egg, and if you have a probe thermometer, give me a reading: that is the quickest teacher.

learned.literature.text: I haven't learned anything yet. I learn how fast your stove boils water when you tap the boil, and your eggs when you tell me how one came out.

learned.pan.text: {water} of water takes about {time} to boil, based on history

example.pan: 12.50 qt of water takes about 6:40 to boil, based on history

learned.forget.more.note: A paragraph opened in place by the (i) beside Forget (UI.md section 4). iOS says the same with learned.forgetExplain.
learned.forget.more.text: This forgets every egg you've told me about and every boil you've timed, and I go back to what's true of eggs in general. You don't need it to undo a wrong answer or two: they wash out after a few more eggs. It's for a new stove, a new kitchen, or a fresh start.

learned.forgetExplain.text: Clears what I've learned from your answers and your boil times. A few wrong answers wash out after a few more eggs anyway; this is for when you'd rather not wait.

learned.confirm.message.text: I forget every egg and how long your water takes to boil, and the times go back to where they started.

feedback.invite.text: Your answers teach me your eggs and your kitchen.

feedback.thanks.text: Thanks. The next egg will use that.

probe.offer.note: E4, the draft in INFERENCE.md section 5 with lowest made highest: when it is read, the middle is the warmest point, so the highest number is the middle and every mistake reads lower.
probe.offer.text: Got a probe thermometer? When I say, push it to the middle of the egg and tell me the highest number you see.

controls.thermometer.ask.note: The checkbox under the Probe thermometer heading. No pronoun: the app is "I" everywhere, so a control the cook taps never speaks as "I".
controls.thermometer.ask.text: Ask for a reading after each egg

probe.now.text: Push the probe to the middle

probe.hint.text: Tell me the highest number you see.

probe.refused.text: That doesn't look like the middle of this egg: expect {low} to {high}. Is the tip in the yolk?

cook.summary.note: {doneness} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.

sousvide.subline.note: {clock} is a time of day, in the locale's own clock.

sousvide.note.whiteBound.text: white still not set, yolk creamy

sousvide.warn.text: At {bath} the white won't set, however long you leave it. I'm built for boiling water, and I'm not reliable below {floor}. Use the pan.

sousvide.hint.text: nothing to start — you are {duration} late

sousvide.start.lastWeekday.note: {weekday} is a weekday name, from weekday.* in this catalogue, in both apps.

alarm.pull.body.text: Straight into the cooling, or the yolk keeps cooking.

alarm.pull.bodyCounter.text: Out of the water and onto the counter.

alarm.cooled.body.text: The carryover is over. That is the egg you asked for.

alarm.probe.body.text: Middle of the egg: tell me the highest number.

activity.target.note: {doneness} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.

activity.summary.note: {doneness} is a doneness word, lower-cased by the app.

activity.note.estimate.text: my guess until you tap Full rolling boil

activity.note.pull.text: into the cooling, or the yolk keeps going

activity.note.done.text: that is the egg you asked for

colophon.lede.text: Times computed from heat conduction and denaturation kinetics, not from a recipe.

colophon.link.text: Source, and the physics it rests on

colophon.ios.text: I work out times from the physics and chemistry of eggs. Both heating and cooling matter for cooking the middle.
